briefing.headline: Impeachment push, devolution talks and census debate dominate politics
briefing.overview: The US House’s failed impeachment of a cabinet secretary highlights partisan divides, while in the UK the government and opposition debate devolution to Wales and census ethnicity options. These stories illustrate key constitutional and political concepts for A‑level study.

stories.title: House impeachment effort fails
stories.what_happened: The House voted down a motion to impeach Pentagon Secretary Hegseth, with most Republicans opposing the measure and most Democrats supporting it. The vote reflects the party‑line split after a midterm loss for Republicans.
stories.why_it_matters: The episode shows how impeachment, a constitutional check on the executive, is used as a political tool, linking to the A‑level focus on the US Constitution and separation of powers.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Democrats say impeachment is necessary to hold the secretary accountable for policy failures.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Republicans claim the move is a partisan revenge plot with no basis in high crimes.

key_term.definition: A constitutional process by which a legislative body can remove a high official for misconduct.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of how constitutional mechanisms can become politicised in an essay on checks and balances.

stories.title: Justice Secretary hints at more Welsh devolution
stories.what_happened: Justice Secretary Alex Norris said Wales could receive additional powers over its justice system, with further discussions on youth justice forthcoming. The announcement follows a commission set up to examine Wales’ constitutional future.
stories.why_it_matters: The story illustrates the evolving nature of the UK’s uncodified constitution and the principle of devolution, a core topic in the A‑level syllabus.

perspectives.label: From the government
perspectives.text: The minister argues extra powers will improve local accountability and address regional needs.

perspectives.label: From the opposition
perspectives.text: Some MPs warn that further devolution could fragment the UK’s legal system.

perspectives.label: From the Welsh perspective
perspectives.text: Plaid Cymru urges swift justice devolution to tackle rising rough‑sleeping among ex‑prisoners.

key_term.definition: The statutory transfer of powers from the central government to regional administrations.

stories.exam_use: Cite as evidence when discussing the flexibility of the UK constitution and the political debate over regional autonomy.

stories.title: MPs call for new census ethnicity options
stories.what_happened: MP Josh Babarinde proposed adding ‘Black English’ and ‘Asian English’ categories to the national census, gaining support from MPs across parties including David Lammy and Sir James Cleverly. The proposal is under consideration by the House of Commons.
stories.why_it_matters: The issue touches on representation, identity politics and the role of Parliament in shaping public policy, linking to the A‑level focus on democracy and participation.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Proponents say the new categories will give a more accurate picture of linguistic diversity.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents worry the changes could complicate data collection and increase costs.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative MPs stress the need for clear, simple census questions.

key_term.definition: A systematic collection of data about a population, used to inform government policy.

stories.exam_use: Use to illustrate how parliamentary debate can shape policy on social inclusion.

stories.title: California rejects billionaire wealth tax
stories.what_happened: California voters turned down a ballot measure that would have imposed a one‑time 5% tax on individuals with net worth over $1 billion. The defeat reflects voter scepticism about new taxes on the wealthy.
stories.why_it_matters: The vote demonstrates direct democracy in the US and raises questions about fiscal policy and wealth redistribution, relevant to the A‑level study of US politics and elections.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Progressive groups said the tax would fund public services and reduce inequality.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Fiscal conservatives warned it would drive capital out of the state and hurt the economy.

key_term.definition: A form of decision‑making where citizens vote directly on policy proposals.

stories.exam_use: Reference when discussing the role of ballot initiatives in US political participation.

stories.title: Scottish Labour calls for EU re‑entry
stories.what_happened: Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra said the UK should re‑join the EU, arguing that solidarity, not separation, is needed and acknowledging the difficulty of the process. The statement adds pressure on Westminster’s EU policy.
stories.why_it_matters: The comment links to debates over the UK’s post‑Brexit relationship with Europe and the influence of regional parties on foreign policy, a key area of the A‑level syllabus.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Labour supporters view EU re‑entry as a way to protect workers’ rights and climate standards.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative critics see it as undermining UK sovereignty.

key_term.definition: A supranational organisation of European states that share policies on trade, law and other areas.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of how sub‑national parties can shape national foreign‑policy debates.

compare.uk: Wales is being offered additional justice powers, reflecting the UK’s flexible, uncodified constitution and ongoing devolution settlements.
compare.us: US states already have independent criminal‑justice systems; further devolution would require constitutional amendment, highlighting a more rigid federal structure.
compare.insight: The contrast shows the UK’s ability to adjust regional powers without formal amendment, whereas US devolution is limited by a written constitution.

ideas_lens.text: The US billionaire tax proposal embodies liberal ideas of using state power to protect individual welfare and curb economic inequality, echoing John Stuart Mill’s advocacy for redistribution. Its defeat illustrates the tension between liberal reform and market‑oriented liberalism.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which devolution in the UK and federalism in the US allow regional governments to influence national policy.
exam_question.tip: Compare the Welsh justice devolution proposal with US state criminal‑justice autonomy, using specific examples to evaluate flexibility versus constitutional constraints.
